methods: Model 1 (published poll averages) applies the five unchanged v19 averaging methods to the v20 dataset: every v19 input poll plus 13 Senate polls and 1 national poll released before or around the freeze and verified afterwards. Raw margins; 30-day window (three most recent polls if fewer); as of Nov 2.

Models 2 and 3 change one thing at a time: dropping polls with partisan or campaign sponsors (either side), symmetrically trimming the three most Republican- and three most Democratic-leaning pollsters, or setting aside pollsters verified to weight on recalled 2024 vote. These are sensitivity checks, not corrections.

Model 4 applies each documented historical polling miss (AAPOR 2016-2024, AAPOR Senate 2022 and 2024, Silver Bulletin 2018 and 2022, the 2025 off-year governor races, the 2021 New Jersey race and the 2024 generic ballot) uniformly to every race. Model 5 shows registered- versus likely-voter versions and turnout-screen scenarios.

Uncertainty: one shared error per simulation (Student-t, 4 degrees of freedom, mean zero, SD from the root-mean-square of past cycle-level misses) plus independent state errors (SD from AAPOR Senate poll errors after removing each cycle's mean and typical sampling error) plus each state average's own sampling noise. 20,000 simulations per setting, fixed seed. No setting assumes polls lean toward either party.

Validation on documented misses and leave-one-cycle-out tests shows the central setting under-covers large past misses (some of which were selected because they were notable). The probabilities are therefore labeled experimental; the historical-scenario seat range is the primary statement of uncertainty.

Context variables (presidential approval, early-vote counts and party-registration shares) are shown with sources and dates and never converted into margin adjustments. Early-vote registration is not candidate support.

Pre-registered tests of the likely-voter and recalled-vote hypothesis (preregistration_mike.json) will be scored once, after certification, with score_v20.js. A pattern by method is observational and cannot by itself prove cause.

Limitations: post-freeze intake covers the named late releases and PollCheck lists checked on Nov 2, not every poll; several fields rest on secondary sources (marked per poll); Siena fieldwork dates and AtlasIntel candidate shares were not readable from Claude's tools; the Nov 1 Michigan endorsement is not measured by any poll.
